newsitem.title: KAZAKHSTAN: Uzbek leader urges support for Afghan warlord.
newsitem.headline: Uzbek leader urges support for Afghan warlord.

text.p: Uzbek President Islam Karimov said on Friday that Afghan warlord General Abdul Rashid Dostum was all that stood between the radical Islamist Taleban militia and the former Soviet republics in Central Asia.

Karimov, speaking at a news conference after a Commonwealth of Independent States (CIS) summit in the Kazakh capital Almaty, said Dostum deserved stronger support from the former Soviet republics neighbouring the war-torn country.
Dostum, an ethnic Uzbek, controls the only highway, including a strategic tunnel, to northern Afghanistan. The Taleban advanced northwards following their capture last week of the capital Kabul.
"If this tunnel is surrendered, they will have no obstacle on their way northwards and we don't know how far they may go," Karimov said
"If we do not want the war to escalate, if we want to force all parties to the negotiating table, we have to make sure that Dostum keeps the tunnel under his control."

There was no indication that the leaders from the three other Central Asian states of Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan and Tajikistan along with Russia shared Karimov's views. Uzbekistan is one of three Central Asian republics that shares a border with Afghanistan.
